equity_bridge.item: CHIPS Act grant + Section 48D ITC receivable (government assistance, current $1,005M + non-current $1,158M)
equity_bridge.note: 10-Q 2026-06-30 GovernmentAssistanceAmountCumulativeCurrent/Noncurrent; cash already earned on past capex, collected outside the modelled flows

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 12.1% diverges >30% from revenue (4.1%) and EPS (-2.0%). Book value grew because earnings were retained into debt-funded 300mm fab capex while buybacks were cut, not because the business compounded; it is rejected as the growth anchor in favour of the through-cycle revenue CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped as TXN is net debt): FY2020 $5,213M, FY2022 $5,584M, FY2025 $2,150M. All are trough-distorted by the FY2023-25 capex supercycle and say nothing about normalised earning power. Owner-FCF CAGRs are ~2-3pp below reported because SBC rose from $224M to $419M while FCF fell -- a growing share of the remaining cash flow is paid in stock.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2026 analog upcycle runs into 2027 (industrial and auto both through prior peaks, destocking done) and then corrects in 2028 the way TI's end markets always have, before mid-cycle growth of 4-6% on rising content per car and per factory. The 300mm fabs earn their keep: capex falls from $4.5B to the guided $2-3B and settles near 8% of revenue, lifting through-cycle pre-SBC EBITDA to ~53% and owner-FCF margins into the low-to-mid 30s -- roughly TI's 2018-2020 cash conversion with SBC charged. China keeps roughly its share of shipments; domestic Chinese competitors take the low end but not the catalog breadth.
scenario_narratives.bull: TI's 300mm cost advantage turns into share: as utilization climbs on already-built capacity, pre-SBC EBITDA reaches ~57.5%, above the FY2022 peak, while capex stays at 6.5-7.5% helped by the remaining $4-6B of CHIPS/ITC benefits. The upcycle is long and shallow (2027 +13%, 2028 flat rather than down), electrification/ADAS and industrial automation compound content growth at 6-8%, and reshoring of Silicon Labs and other fab-light rivals' volumes into TI's fabs reinforces the scale moat.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 rebound proves to be a restock rather than a new cycle: 2027 flat, 2028 -10% as industrial and auto roll over together. With half of shipments landing in China, the anti-dumping probe and export-control retaliation push Chinese OEMs to domestic analog suppliers, and mature-node price pressure caps pre-SBC EBITDA at ~48.5% -- the FY2024-25 trough level -- on a much larger depreciation base. Without further ITC, capex runs at 9% to keep the 300mm network current, and owner-FCF margins settle in the mid-20s.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value TI through the cycle, not at a point in it. The reported FCF of FY2023-25 understates earning power because it carries ~$5B/yr of growth capex for 300mm capacity that is now built; the H1-2026 FCF overstates it because it carries one-off CHIPS cash and an upcycle margin. The component build lets capex taper to a stated steady state, runs one explicit downturn, capitalises a through-cycle margin at a 16x cap appropriate to a cyclical, and counts the CHIPS receivable once in the bridge.
key_risks_to_valuation: China: ~half of shipments end in China; anti-dumping duties or export-control retaliation are not in the base case
Cycle timing: valuing near an upcycle peak -- the 2028 correction could come earlier or be deeper than -5%
Steady-state capex: every 1pp of revenue in perpetual capex is worth roughly $12-14/share
Silicon Labs (~$7.5B cash, H1 2027 close) excluded as NPV-neutral; a failed integration or overpayment is a direct deduction
CHIPS/ITC: the remaining $4-6B management range is only partly credited; policy reversal would remove the netted portion

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 152.73-334.03
data_sources.financials: TXN_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2006-Q2 2026); SEC companyfacts API for depreciation, amortization, short-term investments, debt split (LongTermDebt incl. current portion), government-assistance receivable, diluted shares, equity-award taxes
data_sources.qualitative: TXN_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): Q2 2026 results, Q3 2026 guidance, FY2026 capex guide $2-3B, CHIPS Act/ITC $7.5-9.5B through 2034, Silicon Labs acquisition

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (920M; FY2025 913M). Held FLAT because SBC (plus equity-award withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count. Silicon Labs is an all-cash deal, so no non-SBC issuance is modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement (ShareBasedCompensation $419M) plus taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards ($34M, financing activities); TI publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Cost of equity 9.6% = 4.2% 10y UST + beta ~1.08 x 5.0% ERP; after-tax cost of debt ~3.9% (FY2025 interest paid $542M on ~$14.1B notes, 16% tax); debt ~6% of capital at market -> ~9.0%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclical and China risk are carried in the scenario paths and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are small (offices/warehouses; TI owns ~95% of its fab capacity). Lease cost left inside EBITDA (no separate lease_cost_pct_path) and lease liabilities excluded from net debt -- one treatment, charged once.
inputs.debt_note: Total debt = XBRL LongTermDebt $14,052M at 2026-06-30, which already includes the $1,149M current portion. The CSV/DB TotalDebt of $15,201M adds the current portion a second time (same defect noted for KEYS/NDSN); it was not used. Commercial paper nil.
inputs.cash_note: Cash $3,660M + short-term investments $3,341M at 2026-06-30 (10-Q). Interest income is NOT stripped from the FCF base because TXN is net debt, not net cash; the engine builds unlevered flows from EBITDA, so neither interest income nor interest expense is in the flows and the debt is charged once in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, US, cyclical). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: TXN is a standard operating semiconductor company -> owner-FCF; first valuation, no memory entry to match. Treated as a capex-supercycle name per the AIA.NZ precedent: the FY2023-25 reported FCF ($1.3-2.6B) is depressed by ~$5B/yr of 300mm fab capex, so the base is NOT last_fcf carried forward -- each year is built from components (EBITDA margin, SBC, D&A, capex, cash tax, working capital), with capex tapering from 25.7% of revenue in FY2025 to the guided $2-3B in FY2026 and a steady-state ~8% thereafter. The H1-2026 FCF surge (TTM ~$6.5B) contains ~$1.1B of one-off CHIPS Act cash in Q2 alone; it is NOT extrapolated -- the CHIPS/ITC receivable already on the balance sheet ($2,163M at 2026-06-30) is added once in the equity bridge, and only a modest further ITC on future qualifying capex is netted into the base capex path for FY2026-2030 (~$1.4B cumulative vs the $4-6B management range remaining). Cyclicality is modelled explicitly: FY2026 tracks H1 actuals plus Q3 guidance (~$22B), FY2027 is a late-upcycle year, FY2028 a cyclical correction, then mid-cycle growth -- so the terminal margin is a through-cycle margin (base pre-SBC EBITDA 53% vs FY2018-25 average ~51% and FY2022 peak ~58%, with the 300mm cost advantage lifting it modestly). FY0 = FY2025; year 1 = FY2026, discounted a full year although three quarters are reported (slightly conservative). Buybacks: TI is a repurchaser ($1,477M FY2025 vs $453M SBC incl. taxes), so the flat count is funded. SILICON LABS: ~$7.5B all-cash acquisition expected to close H1 2027 is excluded (standalone TI) and treated as roughly NPV-neutral -- ~$4.4B unaffected value plus ~$450M/yr targeted synergies against a 69% premium and integration costs; on close net debt rises by ~$7.5B and SLAB flows are added.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 = H1 actual $10.29B + Q3 guide midpoint $5.9B + Q4 ~$5.75B = ~$21.9B (+24%). FY2027 late-upcycle +8%; FY2028 cyclical correction -5% (TI has had a down year roughly every 3-4 years: 2009, 2012-13, 2019, 2023-24); then 6% -> 3.5%, in line with the 10yr revenue CAGR (3.1%) plus rising analog content in industrial/auto.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA (OI + D&A + SBC): FY2025 47.7%, H1-2026 53.3%, Q2-2026 ~55%. FY2018-25 average ~51%, FY2022 peak ~58%, troughs ~48%. Base matures at 53% -- the 300mm cost advantage (~40% lower cost per chip) lifts the through-cycle margin ~2pp, partly offset by Chinese mature-node price pressure.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guided $2-3B (H1 $1.19B): ~$2.4B gross = 10.9%, net of ~1.9pp further 48D ITC -> 9.0%. FY2027-30 net 7-7.5% (gross ~8.5-9% less tapering ITC). Steady state 8%: above the 4-6% pre-supercycle norm because 300mm equipment refresh and the larger asset base need more, below the 25%+ peak. D&A rises with fabs placed in service (FY2026 ~$2.3B) and falls toward capex as the peak vintage ages; terminal D&A 7.5% < capex 8% so the terminal year carries no unearned depreciation shield.
base.tax_rationale: GAAP ETR 12.4% FY2025 / 10.8% H1-2026 (FDII/FDDEI, R&D). FY2024-25 cash taxes ($451M/$296M) were depressed by ITC and are not a base. Cash rate 15% stepping to 16% as the ITC tail fades.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: receivables $2.5B + inventory $4.6B - payables $0.7B = ~29% of revenue. Capture -15% on the revenue change (growth consumes cash) -- below the 29% balance-sheet ratio because inventory (196 days, deliberately built ahead of the upturn) can be released.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the valuation date sits late in a sharp upcycle (Q2 revenue +23% YoY, price near the top of its 52-week range) with a regulator-specific risk -- China anti-dumping and export controls over half of shipments -- that the base does not price. Base 50% as the through-cycle path. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things at once: a shallow 2028, margins above the FY2022 peak, and the full CHIPS/ITC range.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
